nodes.description: Mutant TUBB4A is still incorporated into microtubules - this is not a null-allele mechanism - but it changes their behaviour. Live-cell imaging in disease-relevant oligodendrocytes and TIRF microscopy of whole-cell lysates show divergent effects on microtubule polymerization and on integration of the mutant subunit, and the direction and magnitude of those effects track with where a given variant sits on the H-ABC-to-dystonia severity spectrum. Because an oligodendrocyte must extend and maintain a large process arborization to myelinate, a cytoskeleton that polymerizes abnormally compromises the lineage's capacity to differentiate and wrap axons.

nodes.description: In parallel with the white-matter lesion, the caudate, putamen, and cerebellum - especially the vermis - undergo progressive atrophy, while the thalamus and globus pallidus are spared. Serial imaging shows the atrophy developing over years in individual patients rather than being a static hypoplasia. Whether the neuronal loss is a primary consequence of mutant TUBB4A in neurons or is secondary to the white-matter lesion is not settled from human data, but a knock-in mouse carrying the H-ABC p.D249N allele shows both neuronal and glial pathology with altered microtubule dynamics in cortical neurons, which argues for a primary neuronal contribution. This node deliberately does not conform to cns_myelin_failure, because the module's consequence node is axonal degeneration secondary to sheath loss and this is a separate grey-matter arm.

nodes.description: Myelin is never adequately deposited, producing the diffuse central hypomyelination that gives the disorder its leukodystrophy classification. This is hypomyelination rather than demyelination: the deficit is a failure to lay myelin down, and follow-up imaging in some patients shows no progression of myelination over years rather than loss of a normally formed sheath. Its extent is variable, and a minority of patients have focal and milder hypomyelination with partial myelination of the corpus callosum and internal capsule.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint combines three motor systems whose anatomical substrates are the three structures TUBB4A is most highly expressed in. Pyramidal involvement gives spasticity, brisk reflexes, and Babinski signs; extrapyramidal involvement gives rigidity, dystonia, choreoathetosis, and oculogyric crises; cerebellar involvement gives ataxia, intention tremor, and dysmetria; and bulbar involvement gives dysarthria, dysphonia, and swallowing difficulty. Cognition is variably affected and is usually less severely affected than motor function, so a severely motor-disabled H-ABC patient may retain near-intact comprehension. Most patients lose independent ambulation.

evidence.snippet: Progressive neurologic findings reflect involvement of the pyramidal tracts (spasticity, brisk deep tendon reflexes, and Babinski sign), extrapyramidal system (rigidity, dystonia, choreoathetosis, oculogyric crisis, and perioral dyskinesia), cerebellum (ataxia, intention tremor, dysmetria), and bulbar function (dysarthria, dysphonia, and swallowing).
Cognition is variably affected and is usually less severely affected than motor function. The rate of progression varies with disease severity.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant alters beta-tubulin 4A, the brain-specific beta-tubulin isotype whose highest expression is in white matter, cerebellum, and basal ganglia. The regional expression pattern is the simplest available explanation for why a mutation in a ubiquitous cytoskeletal building block produces disease confined to those three structures. The recurrent p.D249N allele accounts for most reported H-ABC; p.C239F and p.R262H are further H-ABC alleles, while p.R2G and p.Q424H at different positions produce the mild dystonia-only end of the spectrum instead.
